propositions: The transition command exposes two distinct force flags with different meanings: valueless --force bypasses start-work gate and --force-close bypasses completion gate, while claim command uses only --force, causing confusion and inconsistent operator interfaces.

Renaming --force-close to --force with context-dependent dispatch resolves the collision: on open->in_progress it bypasses start-work (existing --force behavior), on close transitions it bypasses completion (existing --force-close behavior), with bare --force recording (no reason given) on close to match claim parity.

The hand-rolled flag parser silently skips unknown tokens, so deleting --force-close would cause stale invocations to become silent no-ops; the implementation must explicitly reject both --force-close and --force-close=value with CommandError naming --force to make failures loud.

Concurrent changes after the rename caused defects: scripts/dependency_audit.py landed with unrenamed --force-close in its auto-close argv, and the test suite only validated flag positions positionally rather than parsing through the real _parse_flags, allowing the breakage to survive.
